note: The Rust advisories that are accepted. The gate runs `cargo audit --deny warnings`, so an unmaintained, an unsound or a yanked crate fails the sweep unless it is listed here. A listed advisory is a decision to revisit, not a permanent exemption. cargo-audit 0.23 does not read an audit.toml, so the list is here and the sweep passes each identifier to it.

advisories.severity: none: the crate is not vulnerable, it is no longer maintained
advisories.why: chrono is used to format and parse RFC 3339 timestamps the application generates itself. There is no patched release to move to.
advisories.exercised: Yes, but only on the application's own timestamps. The crate is not exposed to untrusted input in a way that would turn a defect in it into a defect here.
advisories.action: Replace chrono with time or jiff in a future release, which is a deliberate change with its own risk, so it is not done inside a maintenance release.

advisories.why: The affected iterator implementations are in a GTK binding that the Tauri Linux backend pulls in. The application's own code never calls them.
advisories.exercised: No. The crate is not in the macOS or Windows build at all, and the affected functions are not called on any platform.
advisories.action: Move to a Tauri release built on glib 0.20 or later. That exists only in a prerelease of the next major version, which is not something a maintenance release should take.

advisories.severity: none: the crate is not vulnerable, it is no longer maintained
advisories.path: agentops -> tauri -> gtk -> glib -> glib-macros -> proc-macro-error (Linux only)
advisories.why: It is a build-time dependency of the GTK bindings. It never reaches the shipped binary's runtime.
advisories.exercised: No. It is not in the macOS or Windows build at all.
advisories.action: It disappears with the same GTK upgrade as RUSTSEC-2024-0429.
